key_insight: Neutral ethylenediamine reconstructs tin-rich tin–lead perovskite surfaces toward a stoichiometric tin-to-lead ratio, improving electron extraction and suppressing interfacial nonradiative recombination.
engineering_relevance: Controlling passivant protonation and surface defects offers a route to more efficient methylammonium-free perovskite solar cells.
method: Compare neutral ethylenediamine and protonated ethylenediammonium iodide surface reactions.
Use atomistic simulations to probe iodide migration and defect-assisted deprotonation.
Link surface reconstruction to stronger n-type character and electron extraction into C60.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency and simulations showing that subsurface iodide vacancies lower the energetic cost of deprotonation.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish long-term operational stability or scalability of the surface treatment.
paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
